subject: Approval needed: High-availability commitment exception — Zenith Financial
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@zenithfinance.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: high-availability commitment for production launch

Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Zenith is planning a phased go-live for our trading analytics product the week of 2026-09-13. Our compliance and SRE teams require a written availability commitment (four 9s preferred) for the first 60 days post-launch for certain workloads; our procurement team flagged this as a contractual exception to your standard hosted SLA.

We're not asking for a full company-wide four-9s SLA — just a scoped uptime commitment for the two endpoints powering our real-time order feed (order-stream.redwood.example and order-query.redwood.example). We are happy to accept a limited-duration exception, a higher monitoring cadence, and additional incident review commitments.

Attached is our formal request and a comparison to our current contract. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an exception or an alternative (SRE-runbook, reinforced on-call) we can show to our legal team?

Appreciate it — happy to jump on another quick call if helpful.

Alex Geller
Head of Infrastructure, Zenith Financial
alex.geller@zenithfinance.com
+1 415 555 0172

Attachment: zenith_ha_request_20260820.pdf (PDF, 183 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

Looping you all in — Zenith (strategic expansion opportunity) has requested a temporary high-availability commitment (four 9s) scoped to two endpoints for 60 days. Procurement will treat this as an SLA exception and will want formal approval/wording.

Key constraints:
- We cannot change global SLA language without legal sign-off.
- Engineering can offer a scoped SRE playbook + elevated on-call and a dedicated escalation path, and a timeboxed availability objective for specific routes behind a committed capacity profile.

Ask: who can approve a limited exception or sign off on the “supplemental availability commitment” text? I recommend:
1) Product + Eng approve the technical measures (Karthik)
2) Laura approves commercial/Sales-side exception and any credits
3) Legal to finalize the wording (I can coordinate with Zenith legal)

I attached their request and a rough rollback plan they asked for. Will coordinate a short exec summary for Laura if that helps.

Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: prod_rollback_plan.md (Markdown, 5 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: high-availability commitment for production launch

Ben / Laura —

Quick technical read: providing an explicit four-9s commitment for specific endpoints for 60 days is operationally possible but non-trivial. High-level notes:

- We'll need reserved capacity for the routes to make availability predictable (Dedicated pool or guaranteed hosted capacity).
- Recommend enabling prefix KV caching and sticky routing for those endpoints to avoid cold-start losses.
- We should codify an incident runbook and a dedicated paging policy (paging to on-call SRE + escalation to Eng L2).
- We should include a rollback/traffic-shift plan (I reviewed Ben's draft; small edits attached).

Costs: estimated incremental monthly cost ~ +35% for the reserved capacity profile during the 60-day window (ballpark). There is also an operational cost for enhanced monitoring and 24/7 paging.

If commercial signs off on an exception in principle, I can prepare a short technical appendix (2–3 pages) describing the guarantees, the monitoring thresholds, and the fallback behavior.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-comparison-zenith-vs-standard.xlsx (Excel, 26 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks — adding the commercial perspective. A few points:

- Zenith is a high-value renew/expand opportunity; Sales has committed to supporting an exec-level relationship.
- We should avoid open-ended credits. If an availability target is missed, recommend a predefined credit table scoped to the two endpoints and only for the 60-day window.
- Legal will need precise wording (start/end dates, exact endpoints, measurement windows, and excluded events).
- Proposed next step: Laura signs a one-page "exception approval" that authorizes Finance to accept a one-time contract addendum with the credit schedule. Then Legal finalizes wording and we send to Zenith for signature (DocuSign).

I can draft the one-pager and the credit schedule today if we have sign-off on the approach.

-Marissa
VP, Sales Operations

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Ben / team —

I reviewed the materials and agree to a timeboxed, scoped exception for Zenith under the following conditions:

- Exception window: 2026-09-13 through 2026-11-12 (60 days).
- Scope: availability commitment applies only to order-stream.redwood.example and order-query.redwood.example under the traffic profile supplied by Zenith (attached).
- Technical requirements (Karthik): reserved capacity profile, designated on-call roster, and a documented incident runbook. Karthik to provide the tech appendix by EOD Tue 2026-08-25.
- Commercial: use a fixed credit table, max credit exposure capped at 5% of the monthly committed revenue for the period. Marissa to provide the credit table and one-page approval doc by EOD Mon 2026-08-24.
- Legal: draft a one-off contract addendum with explicit start/end dates, measurement windows, exclusions (force majeure, third-party network outages), and an audit clause. Ben, please coordinate Zenith legal and get DocuSign link.

If all of the above are in place and Legal approves the addendum, I authorize Marissa and Finance to accept the contracted terms. This email constitutes executive approval in principle (subject to final Legal wording).

Please treat this as high priority — Ben, confirm you will coordinate Zenith and get them the DocuSign URL once Legal sends the addendum.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial & Partnerships
